response.query: What falsification tests, placebo events, and pre-trend checks will validate instrument exclusion in firm-level and macro-level shrinkflation identification?
response.answer: Falsification tests, placebo events, and pre-trend checks validate instrument exclusion in shrinkflation studies by ensuring no spurious relationships and confirming instruments' relevance. Negative control tests and placebo tests are essential for firm-level and macro-level identification. Pre-trend analysis confirms instruments' validity before treatment effects.

results.title: Falsification Tests | Erin Hartman
results.content: Falsification tests are statistical tests that researchers conduct to marshal evidence that their design is valid their conclusions are sound. Current practice in falsification testing does not allow researchers to provide statistical evidence that their assumptions are warranted. Daniel Hidalgo), argues that falsification tests should be structured so that the responsibility lies with researchers to positively demonstrate that the data is consistent with their identification assumptions or theory. This means that researchers should begin with the initial hypothesis that the data is *inconsistent* with a valid research design, and only reject this hypothesis if they provide sufficient statistical evidence in favor of data consistent with a valid design. Statistical tests of equivalence are a natural way to conduct a falsification test, and allow researchers to provide statistical evidence that their research design is sound and their conclusions are warranted. I have extended this work to the regression discontinuity setting in Equivalence Testing for Regression Discontinuity Designs.

results.content: Falsification tests are statistical tests that researchers conduct to marshal evidence that their design is valid their conclusions are sound. Current practice in falsification testing does not allow researchers to provide statistical evidence that their assumptions are warranted. By failing to detect a problem with the design assumptions, rather than providing evidence of a valid design, researchers conflate statistical insignificance with substantive homogeneity. Statistical tests of equivalence are a natural way to conduct a falsification test, and allow researchers to provide statistical evidence that their research design is sound and their conclusions are warranted. I have extended this work to the regression discontinuity setting in Equivalence Testing for Regression Discontinuity Designs. ### Equivalence Testing for Regression Discontinuity Designs. results.title: DP19127 Negative Control Falsification Tests for Instrumental Variable Designs | CEPR
results.content: ## Secondary Menu. ## User account menu. # DP19127 Negative Control Falsification Tests for Instrumental Variable Designs. We develop theoretical foundations for widely used falsification tests for instrumental variable (IV) designs. We characterize these tests as conditional independence tests between negative control variables — proxies for potential threats — and either the IV or the outcome. We find that conventional applications of these falsification tests would flag problems in exogenous IV designs, and propose simple solutions to avoid this. We also propose new falsification tests that incorporate new types of negative control variables or alternative statistical tests. Finally, we illustrate that under stronger assumptions, negative control variables can also be used for bias correction. results.title: Explaining firm-level reactions to macro shocks | CEPR
results.content: # Explaining firm-level reactions to macro shocks. Understanding differences in firm responses to macroeconomic shocks is key for designing policy actions. This column identifies 67 macro shocks using ‘jump’ days in the US stock market over 2020-2022. It measures firm exposures using individual stock returns and, crucially, discussions of business risk factors in corporate filings. These exposures are largely uncorrelated for different shocks (such as pandemic and inflation shocks) and, collectively, account for most of the rise in cross-firm dispersion in the 2020 recession. To quantify firm-level exposures to each category of macro shocks, we exploit two types of information: stock returns, and prior discussions of business risk factors in mandatory corporate filings.

Title: Level-4 Instrument Control - Why It's Relevant for Part 11 | BioPharm International
The key strengths and weaknesses of different levels of control and feedback for analytical instruments and data transfer systems are highlighted in this article. During the requirements analysis phase of analytical data systems used in regulated environments, one question is frequently posed: Does Part 11 require "compliant instrument control" functions in an analytical data system? What does this mean for instrument control functions in analytical data systems? ### Levels of Instrument Control. In many cases, the data systems used at the time for the evaluation of the analytical measurements did not have any direct instrument control capabilities and data was recorded through an analog-digital converter. We have observed a trend to replace level-1 systems with systems that implement full instrument control. In most cases, manufacturers implement full instrument control (level 3) for their own systems. Some manufacturers have implemented an additional level of instrument capabilities that can be controlled from within the data system. Level-4 instrument control implementations are based on bidirectional, handshake-based communication between the controller and the instrument.
